question: Reena borrowed Rs. 1200 at simple interest for a number of years equal to the rate of interest. At the end of the loan term, she paid Rs. 432 in interest. What was the interest rate?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the number of years (T) equals the rate of interest (R), the formula for Rate simplifies directly to R = √(SI × 100 ÷ P).

⇒ R = √(432 × 100 ÷ 1200)

⇒ R = √(36) = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1200

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹432

Time (T) = Rate (R)

 
 Principal
 ₹1200
 
 
• 
 

 Rate = R%
 Time = R years
 
 
 Interest
 ₹432

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numerical value of the rate of interest be R% and time be R years.

⇒ 432 = (1200 × R × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 432 = 12 × R²

⇒ R² = 432 ÷ 12

⇒ R² = 36

⇒ R = √36 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

When interest is compounded annually, Amount (A) = P(1 + R÷100)T. The compound interest is calculated as CI = A − P.

SI vs CI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for exactly 2 years can be calculated directly using the formula: Difference = P(R÷100)².

Rule of 72

It is a quick calculation method used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual fixed interest rate. Years ≈ 72 ÷ R.
